sources.name: Dhakal, Feit, Kristensson & Oulasvirta (2018), Observations on Typing from 136 Million Keystrokes, CHI 2018
sources.measures: Words per minute on a transcription task of 15 English sentences in an online study hosted with a commercial typing-test site. WPM = (characters in the transcribed string / 5) / minutes from first to last keypress, averaged over sentences. Participants self-selected; 12% excluded for uncorrected error rate above 25% or technical problems. Sample mostly young (mean age 24.5, 75% aged 11-30), 68% from the US, 85% native English speakers, 72% had taken a typing course.
sources.notes: Paper gives mean 51.56 and SD 20.20 for all participants, and defines 'fast typists' as above approx. 78 WPM (faster than 90% of participants) and 'slow typists' as below approx. 26 WPM (slowest 10%). Fast-typist group: mean 89.56, SD 9.53. No p99 is published; the text says the fastest typists reach 120 WPM or more. Distribution described as slightly positively skewed (skewness 0.513, kurtosis -0.11). Data collected over three months in 2016-2017; paper published April 2018. Aalto project page and Cambridge/Aalto news releases repeat these figures and are not independent.

sources.name: TypeLit.io, The State of Typing (updated 16 April 2026)
sources.measures: Per-user average WPM from real typing sessions on TypeLit.io, where users transcribe passages from classic books in 9 languages. Includes users with at least 5 pages typed; users averaging above 150 WPM excluded from most aggregates. Word definition not stated.
sources.notes: Published as threshold shares, not percentiles: 29.9% of users above 60 WPM, 7.3% above 80, 1.3% above 100, 0.1% at 120 or above. The non-standard keys above restate those thresholds as the implied percentile rank (e.g. 100 WPM is exceeded by 1.3% of users). No explicit p99 given. Distribution described as resembling log-normal with a long right tail. Sample is self-selected typing practice users; n stated as '30,000+'.

sources.name: Fastfingers.net, Average Typing Speed & Statistics
sources.measures: Per-test WPM across 7,204,168 timed typing tests on the site (98% are 60-second tests), all languages combined; Indonesian (2.1M tests) and English (2.1M tests) dominate. Scores outside 1-250 WPM excluded. Word definition not stated. Numbers refreshed periodically; no reference date given beyond the 2026 page footer.
sources.notes: Published as bins: 0-19 WPM 15%; 20-39 48%; 40-59 28%; 60-79 8%; 80-99 2%; 100+ 0% (rounded). Page states 10% of tests are 60+ WPM, hence p90 = 60; 2% at 80 or above, hence p98 ≈ 80. English-only average is 33 WPM. Top recorded score 238 WPM. No p99 published; the 100+ bin rounds to 0%, so p99 lies in the 80-99 band on this sample.

definition: Words per minute on a transcription task of 15 English sentences in an online study hosted with a commercial typing-test site. WPM = (characters in the transcribed string / 5) / minutes from first to last keypress, averaged over sentences. Participants self-selected; 12% excluded for uncorrected error rate above 25% or technical problems. Sample mostly young (mean age 24.5, 75% aged 11-30), 68% from the US, 85% native English speakers, 72% had taken a typing course.
caveat: No source publishes an explicit 99th-percentile typing speed. The best academic source (Dhakal et al. 2018, n=168,960) gives mean 51.56 WPM, SD 20.2, and a 90th percentile of about 78 WPM, with the fastest typists at 120+ WPM. Platform data place the top-1% cutoff between roughly 80 WPM (Ratatype, Fastfingers, per-test, large share of beginners and non-English tests) and about 100 WPM (TypeLit, per-user, 1.3% exceed 100). All samples are self-selected online typing-test or typing-practice users, skewed young and towards people interested in typing, not the general population. Per-test and per-user figures differ, test length and error handling vary by site, and the question gives no country, sex or age, so world/all is assumed.

new_metric.label: Typing speed
new_metric.definition: Words per minute on a transcription typing test, where one word is five characters including spaces, measured over a timed test or fixed set of sentences on a physical keyboard.
phrasings: what is a good typing speed
how many words per minute is fast
